newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU assembly urges EU freeze relations with Serbia.
newsitem.headline: EU assembly urges EU freeze relations with Serbia.

text.p: The European Parliament urged the European Union and its individual countries on Thursday to freeze relations with Serbia until democracy had been established there.

In a resolution the parliament said they should "freeze relations with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia until the Belgrade authorities have taken positive steps towards establishing a genuine democracy in Serbia and...Yugoslavia."

It made its demand on the 59th day of protests across Serbia aimed at forcing President Slobodan Milosevic's Socialist government to reinstate annulled November 17 municipal elections in which the opposition won 14 of Serbia's 18 biggest cities.
An Organisation of Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) investigation has recommended that the opposition victories be reinstated.
The European Parliament urged Milosevic "fully and publicly to accept the OSCE's verdict and to guarantee without delay the viability of the independent media and access to those media."
It urged the EU to do what it could to help the independent media.
The parliament cannot force the hand of EU governments, but as the EU's directly elected assembly its message carries moral weight.
It reminded the EU that the bloc's policy is that respect of the rights of minorities is a necessary condition for the establishment of good relations with Belgrade.
